Since the isoelectric point of SnO is ~5.5-6.0, the film deposition is impeded by positive charges on the tin 2 oxide particles and FTO surface at low pH. Capping ligands containing negatively charged carboxylate group like thioglycolic acid (TGA) can bind strongly to nanoparticles, neutralize charges and facilitate their attachment to the FTO substrate, leading to a dense and conformal nanoparticle coating. In the field of dye sensitized solar cells, TGA was widely reported to act as a dual functional linker in the chemical bath deposition of quantum dots (QDs) on zinc oxide surface, where the thiol group was chosen to facilitate binding of CdS QDs to zin oxide. There is, however, no obvious reason for including a thiol functional group for tin oxide CBD, considering the weaker interaction between sulfur and tin compared to oxygen and tin. This statement is Page 25 of 54 DE-EE0009512 Massachusetts Institute of Technology supported by the fact that bond dissociation energy between tin and sulfur (464 KJ/mol)[12] is smaller than that of tin and oxygen (548 KJ/mol). Moreover, TGA is known to cause pinholes and defects in the perovskite layer which negatively affects the long term stability of the devices. Due to the nonvolatile nature of TGA, we infer that TGA as a chemical impurity may remain at the tin oxide/perovskite interface after thermal annealing. Following this logic, we suggest that a volatile dicarboxylic acid is a better alternative to TGA by ensuring connectivity between individual tin oxide nanoparticles and allowing efficient attachment of nanoparticles to the substrate. Furthermore, long term stability of the device may be improved if organic residues can be fully removed by post treatments at a relatively low temperature. Here, we report the use of the volatile and tin-chelating linker molecule oxalic acid (OA) as a replacement to the conventional TGA ligand. We conclude that the ditopic carboxylic acid OA can chemically link the substrate to the particles in the bath solution and accelerate subsequent condensation of colloidal particles. Moreover, volatile OA (sublimation temperature 157 °C) can be removed by thermal annealing and a mild surface treatment with H O . The surface oxygen 2 2 vacancies of the SnO layer are synergistically selectively passivated. The rational design of the x ligand in the chemical bath plus the controlled oxidation of the surface tin oxide layer leads to improved long-term device stability (T85 = 1500 hours) compared to control devices with TGA CBD tin oxide (T80 = 250 hours).
